section_summary: This section contains a largely unreadable Japanese-language propaganda booklet accompanied by an OSS memorandum describing its coverage of the November 1943 “Great East Asia” meeting in Tokyo. It also includes a cross-reference concerning Japanese deportees from Peru and three later withdrawal notices replacing restricted CIA/OSS-related records. The section ends with an FBI letter offering four Japanese publications on military strategy, international affairs, government social assistance, and South America to the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Japanese propaganda booklet and OSS forwarding memorandum
subfiles.from: Bernard A. Towell, OSS X-2 Branch
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal, Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a Japanese propaganda booklet containing the declaration and speeches delivered at the November 6, 1943 “Great East Asia” meeting in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Pages 241-270 appear to comprise the attached booklet, but their OCR is blank or fragmentary and supplies no usable text. The covering memorandum states that the booklet contains a joint declaration and speeches by representatives of Eastern nations at a meeting convened by the Japanese government in Tokyo. The Japanese Legation in Lisbon published it for propaganda purposes.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning the deportation of Santiago Sosuke Sakai and Katsu Ishikawa
subfiles.about: Directs researchers to an original record concerning the deportation of Santiago Sosuke Sakai and Katsu Ishikawa.
subfiles.summary: The sheet cross-references information about the deportation of two named persons from Peru. It identifies the original paper by the file number 740.00115 PW/10-1444.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for restricted record dated November 20, 1944
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a November 20, 1944 item from the file because access to it was restricted.
subfiles.summary: The notice replaces an original document whose identifying information is badly corrupted in the OCR. Its limited metadata appears to refer to G-2 and Neal. The record was withdrawn as security-classified or otherwise restricted CIA/OSS information under authority dated March 13, 1978.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for restricted Chungking record
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a November 29, 1944 item associated with Chungking because access to it was restricted.
subfiles.summary: The notice stands in place of an original record associated with Chungking. The original was removed as security-classified or otherwise restricted CIA/OSS information. The cited restriction authority is dated March 13, 1978.

subfiles.title: Withdrawal notice for restricted Moscow record
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a November 29, 1944 item associated with Moscow because access to it was restricted.
subfiles.summary: The notice replaces an original record associated with Moscow. It states that the item was removed because it contained security-classified or otherwise restricted CIA/OSS information. The cited restriction authority is dated March 13, 1978.

subfiles.title: Information Concerning Japanese Government Activities
subfiles.from: John Edgar Hoover, Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Offers the Department of State four untranslated Japanese books concerning Japanese strategy, international affairs, social policy, and South America.
subfiles.summary: Hoover reports that the FBI has obtained four Japanese-language books published in Tokyo and asks whether the Department of State wishes to examine them. The works discuss Japan's war against China, possible conflict with Russia, Vladivostok's defenses, Japanese diplomacy and internal reorganization, social-assistance administration, and South American economic and social affairs. One book also describes possible United States Army and Navy troop movements to the Philippines, Alaska, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, and the Panama Canal Zone. Copies of the information were furnished to economic, naval-intelligence, and War Department authorities.
